question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.


All these things happen/ because she do not / pay heed to my words.
options: All these things happen
No error
because she do not
pay heed to my words
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "because she do not"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "because she do not" due to a violation of the Subject-Verb Agreement rule.
☛ "She" is a third-person singular subject, so it must take the auxiliary verb "does" instead of "do".
☛ Correct structure: "because she does not".
☛ This mistake is frequently tested in exams as students often confuse "do" and "does" with singular/plural subjects.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular subjects (he/she/it) require verbs with s/es (e.g., goes, does).
☛ Example:
- Incorrect: He play football.
- Correct: He plays football.
☛ Usage of Do/Does:
- "Do" for plural subjects (I/we/you/they).
- "Does" for singular subjects (he/she/it).

Example:
Incorrect - because she do not care.
Correct - because she does not care.

☛ "She" एक third person singular subject है, इसलिए इसके साथ "do" नहीं बल्कि "does" का प्रयोग होना चाहिए।
☛ Correct structure: "because she does not" (क्योंकि वह नहीं)।
☛ यह गलती Competitive Exams में अक्सर पूछी जाती है, क्योंकि छात्र "do/does" का प्रयोग Subject के अनुसार भूल जाते हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Singular subjects (he/she/it) के साथ singular verb (V1 + s/es) का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ Example:
- Incorrect: She go to school.
- Correct: She goes to school.
☛ "Do/Does" का प्रयोग:
- Plural subjects (I/we/you/they) के साथ "do"।
- Singular subjects (he/she/it) के साथ "does"।

Example:
Incorrect - because she do not listen.
Correct - because she does not listen.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Harish says / that his sister / loves to play / harmonium.
options: Harish says
harmonium
loves to play
that his sister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "harmonium"

Explanation:
☛ The word harmonium is incorrect in the given sentence because it refers to a musical instrument.
☛ As per English grammar rules, musical instruments always take the definite article 'the' before them.
☛ The correct phrase should be: "loves to play the harmonium" since it specifies a particular instrument.
☛ In such error spotting questions, special attention must be paid to articles, especially with musical instruments, superlatives, or unique objects.

Grammar Rules:
☛ The definite article 'the' is used for specific objects/people that are already known.
☛ Always use 'the' with musical instruments: "She plays the violin" (correct), "She plays violin" (incorrect).
☛ Exceptions to this rule are sports (cricket, hockey etc.) where no article is used: "He plays football".

Example:
Incorrect - "She plays flute"
Correct - "She plays the flute"

☛ अंग्रेजी व्याकरण के नियमों के अनुसार, musical instruments के नाम से पहले definite article 'the' का प्रयोग होता है।
☛ सही वाक्य होगा: "loves to play the harmonium" क्योंकि यहां specific instrument का जिक्र है।
☛ इस तरह के error spotting प्रश्नों में articles का विशेष ध्यान रखना चाहिए, खासकर जब musical instruments, superlative degrees या unique things का उल्लेख हो।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Definite Article 'the' का प्रयोग विशेष वस्तुओं/व्यक्तियों के लिए होता है जो पहले से ही ज्ञात हों।
☛ Musical instruments के साथ हमेशा 'the' article का प्रयोग करें: "She plays the guitar" (सही), "She plays guitar" (गलत)।
☛ इस नियम के अपवाद हैं sports (क्रिकेट, हॉकी आदि) जहां article का प्रयोग नहीं होता: "He plays cricket"।

Example:
Incorrect - "He plays piano"
Correct - "He plays the piano"

question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

The boy told his mother that he saw the most tall giraffe at the zoo.
options: The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo."

Explanation:
☛ Superlative Degree is required because we are comparing one giraffe to all others.
☛ most tall is incorrect as "tall" is a monosyllabic adjective, whose superlative form is "tallest", not most tall.
☛ Double Superlative (most tallest) and Double Comparative (more taller) are grammatically incorrect.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Monosyllabic Adjectives (e.g., tall, fast) take -est to form superlatives (e.g., tallest).
☛ Polysyllabic Adjectives (e.g., beautiful) use most (e.g., most beautiful).
☛ Double Superlative/Comparative (e.g., most tallest, more better) are always wrong.

Example:
Incorrect - The boy saw the most tall giraffe.
Correct - The boy saw the tallest giraffe.

☛ most tall गलत है क्योंकि "tall" एक monosyllabic adjective (एक-अक्षर विशेषण) है, जिसका superlative form "tallest" होता है, न कि most tall।
☛ Double Superlative (most tallest) और Double Comparative (more taller) ग्रामर के नियमों के अनुसार गलत हैं।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Monosyllabic Adjectives (जैसे tall, fast, big) के लिए -est लगाकर superlative बनाया जाता है।
☛ Polysyllabic Adjectives (जैसे beautiful, intelligent) के लिए most का प्रयोग किया जाता है (उदाहरण: most beautiful).
☛ Double Superlative/Comparative (जैसे most tallest, more better) हमेशा गलत होते हैं।

Example:
Incorrect - The boy saw the most tall giraffe.
Correct - The boy saw the tallest giraffe.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Throughout my career as a journalist, / I covered many important stories and / interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me / to share important information and insights with my readers.
options: I covered many important stories and
interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me
to share important information and insights with my readers
Throughout my career as a journalist,
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The phrase "which allow me" is incorrect because "which" is a relative pronoun referring to "numerous individuals" (plural), and it should take a plural verb. However, the verb "allow" should be in the past tense ("allowed") to match the overall past context of the sentence.
☛ Correction: "which allowed me" is correct since the entire sentence describes past experiences of a journalist.
☛ Grammar Rule: The verb after a relative pronoun must agree in number and tense with its antecedent.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Relative Pronouns: Relative pronouns (who, which, that) introduce dependent clauses, and their verbs must agree with their antecedents in number and tense.
☛ Tense Consistency: If the main clause is in the past tense, the relative clause should also use the past tense. Here, "covered" and "interviewed" are in the past tense, so "allowed" is required instead of "allow".
☛ Plural vs. Singular: If the antecedent is plural, the verb must be plural. Here, "individuals" is plural, so "allow" (plural) is correct, but it should be "allowed" in the past tense.

Example:
Incorrect - The books which is on the table are mine.
Correct - The books which are on the table are mine.

☛ Correction: "which allowed me" सही होगा क्योंकि पूरा वाक्य journalist के past experiences के बारे में बता रहा है।
☛ Grammar Rule: Relative pronoun (which, who, that) का verb उस noun के number और tense के अनुसार होना चाहिए जिसे वह refer कर रहा है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Relative Pronouns: Relative pronouns (who, which, that) dependent clauses introduce करते हैं और उनका verb उनके antecedent (पहले आए noun) के अनुसार agree करता है।
☛ Tense Consistency: यदि main clause past tense में है, तो relative clause भी past tense में होना चाहिए, जैसे यहाँ "covered" और "interviewed" past tense में हैं, इसलिए "allowed" होगा, न कि "allow"।

Example:
Incorrect - The books which is on the table are mine.
Correct - The books which are on the table are mine.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

With cloud streaming, people can play games from a / internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey / dedicated hardware such as a game console.
options: With cloud streaming, people can play games from a
No error
dedicated hardware such as a game console
internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "With cloud streaming, people can play games from a"

Explanation:
☛ The error lies in "from a" because the phrase "internet-connected device" requires the indefinite article 'an' instead of 'a'.
☛ The word "Internet" starts with a vowel sound ('I'), so the correct article is 'an'.
☛ Correct phrase: "from an internet-connected device".
☛ Other parts (avoiding the need for pricey dedicated hardware such as a game console) are error-free.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Articles (a/an): 'A' is used before words with a consonant sound, while 'an' is used before words with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u).
☛ Example:
Incorrect: "It is a apple."
Correct: "It is an apple." (Since 'apple' starts with vowel sound 'a').

Example:
Incorrect - With cloud streaming, people can play games from a internet-connected device.
Correct - With cloud streaming, people can play games from an internet-connected device.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.


The fight of the cobra and the mongoose / is a classic drama often seen in India, / and the outcome was largely the same.
options: and the outcome was largely the same
The fight of the cobra and the mongoose
No error
is a classic drama often seen in India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "and the outcome was largely the same"

Explanation:
☛ In the given sentence, the phrase "and the outcome was largely the same" has a tense inconsistency.
☛ The first two parts (The fight of the cobra and the mongoose is a classic drama often seen in India) are in present tense, while the third part (and the outcome was largely the same) is in past tense.
☛ Since the entire sentence describes a general truth, "was" should be replaced with "is" to maintain tense consistency.
☛ "Largely the same" is grammatically correct as it correctly combines an adverb (largely) with an adjective (same).

Grammar Rules:
☛ Tense Consistency: Tense should remain uniform in a sentence or paragraph, especially when stating facts or habits.
☛ Adverb Usage: Largely (adverb) appropriately modifies same (adjective).
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: Outcome (singular) agrees with was (singular past) or is (singular present).

Example:
Incorrect - The Earth revolves around the sun and the moon was a satellite.
Correct - The Earth revolves around the sun and the moon is a satellite. ------

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

As they driven through the dark, twisting lane / down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard / the whistling of the night air in his ears.
options: As they driven through the dark, twisting lane
down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard
the whistling of the night air in his ears.
No error
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "As they driven through the dark, twisting lane"

Explanation:
☛ Error: The verb "driven" is incorrect here as it is a past participle (V3), but the sentence requires the past tense (V2) form.
☛ Correct Verb Form: Since the sentence is in the past tense, "drove" (V2) should be used instead.
☛ Subject-Verb Agreement: The subject "they" is plural, so the plural verb "drove" is appropriate.
☛ Context: The sentence describes a past action (driving through a lane), which mandates the use of past tense.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Past Tense vs Past Participle: Past tense (V2) is used for independent actions, while past participle (V3) is used in perfect tenses or passive voice.
☛ Examples:
Incorrect - As they written the letter
Correct - As they wrote the letter
☛ Common Mistakes: Students often misuse past participles like "driven", "written" as past tense verbs, which is grammatically incorrect.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Understand the difference between Adjective and Noun:

- Nouns (e.g., "viability") act as subjects/objects in sentences.
☛ Prepositional Phrases (e.g., "of life") require a noun before them.

Example:
Incorrect - The viable of life is uncertain.
Correct - The viability of life is uncertain.

☛ "Viable" एक adjective है, जिसका अर्थ है "सक्षम" या "जीवनक्षम"। लेकिन यहाँ noun की आवश्यकता है।
☛ सही शब्द "viability" (संज्ञा रूप) होना चाहिए, क्योंकि यह "life" से सम्बंधित है।
☛ The viability of life सही संरचना है, जिसका अर्थ है "जीवन की संभावना"।
☛ Adjective को noun की तरह प्रयोग करना व्याकरणिक त्रुटि है।

Grammar Rules:
☛ Adjective और Noun का सही प्रयोग समझें:
- Adjective (जैसे "viable") किसी noun को modify करता है, लेकिन स्वयं subject/object नहीं बन सकता।
- Noun (जैसे "viability") वाक्य में subject/object का कार्य करता है।
☛ Prepositional Phrase में noun की आवश्यकता होती है (जैसे "of life" के पहले)।

Example:
Incorrect - The viable of life is uncertain.
Correct - The viability of life is uncertain.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Why don’t / you throw this / paper on the dust bin?
options: paper on the dust bin
No error
you throw this
Why don’t
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is "paper on the dust bin"

Explanation:
☛ The phrase "paper on the dust bin" contains an error.
☛ The incorrect use of preposition "on" is the mistake. The correct preposition for throwing something inside a bin is "into".
☛ "On" implies placement on a surface (e.g., The cup is on the desk), while "into" indicates movement towards the inside (e.g., Put the toys into the box).
☛ Since the action involves throwing the paper inside the dustbin, "into the dust bin" is grammatically accurate.

Grammar Rules:
☛ Prepositions establish relationships between words in a sentence.
☛ on → Refers to a surface (The cat sat on the mat).
☛ into → Indicates movement towards the interior (She walked into the room).
☛ Competitive exams often test contextual usage of prepositions.

Example:
Incorrect - He placed the files on the cabinet.
Correct - He placed the files into the cabinet.
